digest.component_or_area: test infrastructure / subprocess and network timeouts
propositions: Blanket autouse _short_timeout fixture (1s call/grace/drain) on test_acli_subprocess_timeout.py causes five real-subprocess reap tests to burn ~1s wall-clock waiting for deadline expiry, creating brittle timing dependencies on interpreter startup speed.

Three reap tests assert on child-side setup (grandchild pidfile, spawn counter, partial stdout) that must complete before timeout fires, but ordering depends only on 1s window exceeding interpreter startup rather than explicit sequencing, creating a wall-clock race on loaded runners.

test_run_acli_429_retries_with_rate_limit_backoff inherits the 1s ceiling and must complete two sequential python spawns within it, creating a latent load flake in the opposite direction that naive shrinking would worsen.
tight_stall fixture injects a 2s low-speed window for throughput testing even though sibling dribble test already proves git honors a 1s window, wasting test time.

Reap tests need explicit readiness gates (child-side marker files polled by parent) rather than relying on injected timeout window to exceed setup time, decoupling test pass conditions from runner load.
